```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence shows real money already spent. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for a compliance tool in March 2026, and the Town of Templeton received a $2,510 AudioEye quote. A has no example of anyone paying for the specific mechanic, and its own Case Against cites 100% churn of paying customers on a closely related SaaS.",
    "B's pain has a cited, dated external trigger: the DOJ compliance deadlines of April 2027 and April 2028, sourced to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. A's pain rests on one Reddit post, and that parent is weighing conversation classes, not specifically an app.",
    "B has a published low-end price point that suits a scanner-only MVP. GovAccess charges $149/month and uses a free-audit lead magnet a solo operator with agents could copy cheaply. A's channels are either costly (about $4.70 CPI for an app whose kids' retention is described as weak) or untested (organic expat groups with no conversion data).",
    "A carries risks the brief documents and does not resolve. Paying Dinolingo parents report kids 'zoning out' on repetitive content. Voiczy already holds the identical positioning. Recording children's voices triggers COPPA and GDPR-K parental-consent overhead.",
    "B also has serious weaknesses, so the edge is relative. Slow municipal procurement threatens the 90-day window, liability exposure on compliance claims is unresolved, and the deadline has already slipped once. Still, B's evidence that buyers pay under pressure is materially stronger than anything in A."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's second demand quote comes from Voiczy's founders on Voiczy's own marketing site. It is a competitor's sales copy, not independent buyer demand. With it discounted, A's demand evidence comes down to a single Reddit parent who is weighing several options, including live classes rather than an app.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B has stronger payment evidence but a real risk of missing the 90-day target because of municipal procurement cycles. The brief offers no evidence on whether a sub-$150/month purchase can skip the RFP process. B's conference booth costs also come from a stale 2015 prospectus. A's consumer model could, in principle, land a first payment faster, but the brief offers no evidence that anyone pays and stays."
}
```
